description.value: The Mayne Island Museum is housed in the original 1896 Plumper Pass Gaol — one of the oldest surviving structures on the island — and tells the stories of First Nations, Japanese, and European settlers who shaped island life. A separate Dalton Deacon Barn adjacent to the gaol holds donated farm machinery and larger heritage pieces. Two digital collections, including the John Aitken Historic Photograph Collection, extend the museum's reach for visitors and researchers alike.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is available and confirms the museum at 424 Fernhill Road, Mayne Island, BC — matching the OSM address. The site describes the museum as a small historic gaol building (1896) operated by the Mayne Island Agricultural Society, with no mention of bike parking, washrooms, water, or any cycling-specific amenities. The community field in the OSM record reads 'Sidney', which appears to be a geographic misclassification since the museum is clearly on Mayne Island, not in Sidney.
concerns: OSM community field is 'Sidney' but the museum is on Mayne Island — these are distinct communities; the record may be geographically miscategorized in the source data.
No phone number available in OSM or on the website; contact is email-only (mayneislandmuseum@gmail.com).
None of the WWC required criteria (bike parking, washrooms, water) could be confirmed from the website — an on-site or in-person verification is recommended before publishing the listing.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, actively operated heritage attraction on Mayne Island with cultural depth — a natural stop for touring cyclists doing a Gulf Islands loop. No required criteria are confirmed, but the attraction value is clear and a manual site visit could verify amenities.
